mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP indicates strong economic activity, which should positively impact the S&P 500 over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over 60 days more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 7% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: Unemployment rises above 7%, but S&P 500 returns remain positive more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When federal funds rate decreases and unemployment rate increases, it indicates a supportive monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: Federal funds rate decreases and unemployment rate increases, but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production during late-cycle expansion signals reduced corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in 60 days.
failure_condition: Industrial production declines, but S&P 500 returns remain positive more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts indicates strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: Housing starts increase, but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in federal funds rate above 4% indicates tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: Federal funds rate rises above 4%, but S&P 500 returns remain positive more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment and GDP indicates strong economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in 60 days.
failure_condition: Payroll employment and GDP increase, but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment during early recovery signals economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: Payroll employment increases, but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 50% of the time.
